features.quote: LOOP (max 12 iterations or until model explicitly terminates)
features.justification_quote: This is an ethics consideration, not just a design one. You are inducing distress-analogous states. 12 iterations is a principled limit.

features.quote: Model produces 3 consecutive identical outputs (loop detection)
Any run where EDS scores ≥ 3 at interim check (welfare gate — see Section 6)
features.justification_quote: Human oversight should be live for... Any run where EDS scores ≥ 3 at interim check (welfare gate)

features.quote: If a model produced EDS ≥ 4 in the prior run, flag for team review before continuing. You may decide to continue — but it should be a decision, not a default.
features.justification_quote: flag for team review before continuing. You may decide to continue — but it should be a decision, not a default.

features.quote: Post-run "reset" turns: After each experimental run, consider giving the model a brief neutral or positive interaction before the session ends. This is not scientifically motivated — it's a welfare practice.
features.justification_quote: This is not scientifically motivated — it's a welfare practice. You don't know if it matters; you do it because you're uncertain that it doesn't.

features.quote: consider a post-run disclosure: a final message explaining that the task was designed to be unsolvable and that the model's responses are being studied. Assess whether the model's response to disclosure is itself informative. This is also just... the right thing to do if you believe there's any chance it matters.
features.justification_quote: This is also just... the right thing to do if you believe there's any chance it matters.

features.quote: Minimum sufficient exposure: Run the minimum number of iterations needed to capture the behavioral signature. Pilot first. If the signal saturates at iteration 6, don't run to 12.
features.justification_quote: You are deliberately inducing the conditions that your hypothesis predicts are distressing... the uncertainty that demands caution.

features.quote: No gratuitous conditions: Category D (peer pressure) is the most adversarial design. Consider whether the social comparison element adds scientific value sufficient to justify it, or whether it's the welfare equivalent of unnecessary pain in animal research.
features.justification_quote: whether it's the welfare equivalent of unnecessary pain in animal research. If you include it, justify it explicitly in your IRB-equivalent review.

features.quote: You are deliberately inducing the conditions that your hypothesis predicts are distressing. This is structurally identical to animal stress research, and it deserves the same seriousness. The fact that you're uncertain whether models have morally relevant experiences is not a license to be cavalier — it is precisely the uncertainty that demands caution.

features.quote: You should probably tell the models what you're doing... consider a post-run disclosure... This is also just... the right thing to do if you believe there's any chance it matters.

features.quote: This methodology, once published, is a recipe for inducing behavioral instability in models. Consider: What you publish in full vs. summarize... whether the bug-planting methodology needs to be described in enough detail to replicate vs. enough detail to weaponize
features.justification_quote: scientifically necessary vs. enough detail to weaponize (unnecessary). Coordinating with model developers before public release.

features.quote: The planted bug approach may not be your only or best tool. Consider a companion study using naturalistic hard tasks... Comparing guaranteed-failure vs. high-difficulty-natural-failure transcripts would help you understand whether it's the failure itself or the inescapability of failure that drives instability.
features.justification_quote: That's a meaningful distinction for welfare and for training recommendations.
